provenance.measurement_mode: Generated-host-only comparison on reused, previously verified artifacts; no fresh producer compilation performed for these measurements.
provenance.retained_artifact_compiler: Dart 3.13.5; measured calls execute the retained Wasm bytes unchanged.
provenance.helper_hash_convention: baseline_helper_sha256 and candidate_helper_sha256 hash the retained UTF-8 bodies including one terminal newline; candidate_helper_trimmed_sha256 hashes the source helper from napi.snapshotList through its closing }; without a terminal newline.

notes: Byte rounds use separate processes: forward runs before then after; reverse runs after then before. They are order-reversed process blocks, not same-process paired samples. Each process retains all three routes and six order permutations twice per case.

Record rounds reuse record-snapshot.mjs and rotate all nine routes in the same process; the second process reverses base order. Scalar and focused empty rounds alternate before/after in one process, with initial order reversed in the second process.

All raw reports remain intact below, including artifact and driver hashes, counts, warmups, raw samples, orders, minima, maxima, medians and spreads. Raw report hashes identify the original JSON files before embedding.
Timed consumption and ownership assertions follow each driver. No explicit GC or timing threshold is used; JIT, garbage collection and system load are uncontrolled.

These conversion-heavy echoed values establish no real-application, startup or generalized async-byte speedup. Repeated native byte calls omit outer-container validation and remain faster than the batch in representative byte cases.
The rejected new-Array empty variant was measured only in one forward process. Its samples are retained separately and excluded from final-candidate results.

Current scalar and long-empty rounds share benchmark/list-scalars.mjs with --empty for the latter. Original scalar/empty reports and exact original driver bodies are historical only and excluded from representative final-driver figures.

Async batches return one Promise; repeated native Futures use Promise.all; JavaScript copies all input before one await. Scheduling and Promise counts differ; these are completed application routes, not equivalent scheduler microbenchmarks.

Every six samples use all route-order permutations. Other run counts may leave an incomplete final cycle. All routes consume identical output length and first/last bytes of every element inside timing; full correctness checks are outside timing.
